question.text: Some historians believe this tsar lost his sanity when his wife died in 1560. His son Feodor's unsuccessful reign led to the Time of Troubles.
question.clue: He called the first Zemsky Sobor, and he had his private army of Oprichniks harass the boyars.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about leaders with titles in common.
swap.text: Give the title last held by Nicholas II of Russia before he was killed in 1918.
swap.clue: It's not in Germany, but one holder of this title issued the Anti-Semitic May Laws, which prohibited the creation of new towns by Jews.

question.text: This first leader of the U.S.S.R. fittingly wrote the introduction to the second edition of Ten Days That Shook the World.
question.clue: This man called for unifying all of his nation's banks into one single bank in his "April Theses," which was written during his sealed train ride returning from exile.

swap.leadin: This leader may have had her husband, Peter III, killed, so that she could take the throne.
swap.text: Name this 18th century Empress of Russia, an "enlightened despot" who supported the works of Voltaire and Diderot while brutally crushing uprisings like Pugachev's Rebellion.
swap.clue: This ruler's private art collection led to the founding of the Hermitage Museum.

question.leadin: One work about this event was later banned in the Soviet Union for emphasizing Leon Trotsky's role and devaluing Joseph Stalin's role in this event.
question.text: Name this event which featured an assault on the Winter Palace. This late 1917 event resulted in the dissolution of Alexander Kerensky's provisional government and the later establishment of the Soviet Union.
question.answerHtml: October Revolution [or Bolshevik Revolution; or Red October; accept synonyms for revolution such as coup; prompt on Russian Revolution]
question.clue: Alexander Kerensky's cadets in Petrograd failed to hold the Winter Palace near the beginning of this event.

swap.leadin: Name some key aspects about the Eastern Front during WWII.
swap.text: The German 6th army was surrounded and forced to surrender at the conclusion of this battle near the Volga River. The city where this battle took place was originally named Tsaritsyn.
swap.clue: After being encircled by a pincer movement, Nazi High Command suggested an ultimately disastrous "air bridge" be used to supply the German Sixth Army.

question.leadin: He was a sworn brother of the Khan of the Golden Horde, to whom he paid tribute.
question.text: Name this Grand Prince of Vladimir and Novgorod, a Russian national hero who fought the Teutonic Knights.
question.clue: He later sought the help of Sartak to oust his brother Andrew from power and allowed for a census and tax collection to be imposed by the Tatars in exchange for the protection of Batu Khan's armies.

swap.text: Novgorodian pirates known as Ushkuyniks plied this long Russian river, attacking cities on it such as Kazan and Astrakhan. This river was the main conduit of trade between the Rus and Sassanid Persia.
swap.clue: Flowing through Nizhniy Novgorod and Samara, this river's canal to the Don provides the most direct connection between the Sea of Azov (AH-soff) and the world's largest lake.

question.leadin: Conspiracy theories held that this ruler became a hermit named Feodor Kuzmich after his mysterious death from typhus in Taganrog.
question.text: Name this tsar, the first one advised by liberal statesman Mikhail Speransky. This tsar conquered Finland and granted a constitution to Poland.
question.clue: After his nation lost the Battle of Friedland, he met with Napoleon on a raft in the Niemen River to sign the Treaty of Tilsit.

swap.text: This capital of the USSR was the site of the 1980 Olympics, as well as frequent "physical culture" parades in Red Square.
swap.clue: This city traces its history to a post founded by Yuri of the Long Arm.

question.text: A founder of the Free Economic Society, this military officer, adviser, and lover of Catherine's planned the coup that brought her to power. He went insane after having lost favor for botching a diplomatic mission to Turkey.
question.clue: This man who was involved in the Free Economic Society and the reform of the law code, a Russian officer who, as lover of Catherine the Great, engineered the coup to put Catherine on the throne.

swap.text: Finally, after 9,289 kilometers and six days and four hours, your trip comes to an end in this city, the terminus of the Trans-Siberian Railway in Russia located on the Sea of Japan.
swap.clue: This city on the Golden Horn Bay near the Russian borders with China and North Korea is located at the eastern terminus of the Trans-Siberian Railroad.

question.leadin: This political party formed in 2001 through a merger of the Fatherland-All Russia and the Unity parties.
question.text: Name this Russian political party that presently controls about 75% of the Duma. It is usually described as a non-ideological "party of power," though its stated ideology is "Russian Conservatism."
question.clue: Nazarbayev is also the chairman of the Nur Otan party, which in 2015 signed a cooperation agreement with this largest political party in Russia, whose incoherent ideology can best be described as "pro-Putin".

swap.leadin: The October Manifesto, a guarantee of reforms drafted following the 1905 Revolution, promised to create this legislative body.
swap.text: Name this legislative body that served as the lower house of the parliament of the Russian Empire, under the State Council. It shares its name with the lower house of the modern Russian Federation's Federal Assembly.
swap.clue: Alexis Aldadin formed the Trudoviks to stand for election to this body.

question.leadin: Name some groups of people whom Peter the Great interacted with.
question.text: After visiting the West, Peter imposed a beard tax on this group of nobles as part of his effort to modernize and civilize their habits.
question.clue: To undermine the influence of these people, a tsar introduced a system in which collegiate registrars were graded "K-14."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about St. Olga of Kiev.
swap.text: This historical redaction by Nestor, which covers the ninth through twelfth centuries, is the main source for the biography of Olga.
swap.answerHtml: Primary Chronicle [or Tale of Past Years; or Pověstĭ Vremęnĭnyhŭ Lětŭ]
swap.clue: This text attributed to the monk Nestor. In another story from this text, Vladimir the Great rejects converting to Islam due to his love of drinking and pork.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a Russian boyar.
question.text: This man took power after returning to Russia in 1619 and being given the name "Great Sovereign." He would go on to rule as a patriarch until he was succeeded by his more famous son Michael.
question.clue: This father of Michael Romanov returned to Russia after the Peace of Deulino in 1619, whereupon he was given the title "Great Sovereign" and assumed power until his death in 1633.

swap.text: The leader of the pro-German government, Pavlo Skoropadskyi, revived the use of this title while leading Ukraine in 1918. This title was traditionally used by leaders of a sich until abolished by Catherine the Great.
swap.clue: Holders of this title, who carried a gem-encrusted mace called a bulawa ("boo-WAH-va"), were elected by the Sich ("seetch") Rada.

question.text: The "green army" is the name sometimes given to Aleksandr Antonov's forces during this rebellion. This peasant rebellion took place during the Russian Civil War and was ended by Mikhail Tukhachevsky.
question.clue: This rebellion, which was suppressed with a force of one hundred thousand Red Army troops under Mikhail Tukhachevsky, who used tactics like firing poisonous gas at peasant strongholds.

swap.leadin: Name these things about Alexander Scriabin's uncle, Vyacheslav Scriabin, FTP each.
swap.text: As a member of the Politburo Molotov was the key signatory, behind Beria, of the order that caused this execution of 25,000 Poles near the namesake area in 1940.
swap.clue: As head of the NKVD, Beria was responsible for masterminding this execution of captive Polish officers in the namesake site in 1940.
